summary: Post-org-merge usage not attributed to new org API key causing credits undercount
description:
Issue summary: After BrightAssist performed an org merge (child org -> parent org) via our console runbook, a subset of usage for the merged API keys is not attributed to the resulting org. Impact: customer invoices and console usage dashboards show ~18% less token usage for the merged org during the post-merge window (2026-03-09 02:00 - 2026-03-10 08:00 UTC). This undercount affects billing reconciliation and quota enforcement.

Environment: prod-us-east (primary), affected stack components: usage ingestion pipeline, org-service merge job, attribution map in billing service.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Perform org merge on staging using the org merge runbook with a dataset that includes active API keys performing streaming generation.
2) Observe usage attribution table in console and compare per-api-key totals pre/post-merge.
3) Query raw events in blob store for timestamps around merge and compare attributed_org_id field.

Observed behavior: A subset of usage events are written with attributed_org_id set to the old (now-merged) org_id or left null. Console aggregate tiles for the merged org therefore show lower usage. Billing pipeline drops or defers those events from per-org rollups leading to undercount on invoice preview.

Expected behavior: All post-merge events should be normalized to the target org_id and immediately included in merged-org rollups and billing previews.

Workaround: Manual re-run of the attribution backfill job for the merge window re-attributes most events; customer requested a backfill which Support initiated (see comments).
